page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eadsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a 3780 GB local disk and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not feature any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top 10%. Multi-threaded performance is also robust, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and database operations fall into the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks. For machine learning workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds with small 135M models, but text generation for large 70B models is poor, falling into the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E64-32ads_v7 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local storage capacity, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dedicated GPU acceleration. The combination of a high-frequency AMD EPYC processor and large memory capacity makes this server appropriate for large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems, data compression tasks, and web serving. However, the lack of a GPU and poor large-model inference speeds make it unsuitable for heavy deep learning or large language model text generation.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-32ads_v7 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine from the Eadsv7 family, powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores), 512.0 GB of RAM, and a 3780 GB local disk. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, this server delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression speeds, alongside strong PassMark CPU and memory scores. However, its multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth are average. While it excels at small-model text generation, large-model LLM inference is a notable performance bottleneck. This configuration is appropriate for memory-intensive workloads, in-memory databases, and data compression tasks, offering a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local storage without GPU acceleration.
